literal: Those of evil deeds do not fear; noble people fear the delusion called evil deed.
translation: Those who habitually commit evil do not fear it, but noble people dread the delusion of committing an evil deed.
modern: தீய செயல்களைச் செய்பவர்கள் அதற்கு அஞ்சமாட்டார்கள்; ஆனால் மேன்மையானவர்கள் தீவினை என்று சொல்லப்படும் செருக்கிற்கு (மன மயக்கத்திற்கு) அஞ்சுவார்கள்.
explanation: This couplet contrasts how different people view harmful actions. Those who are already accustomed to doing wrong do not fear the consequences of their actions. In contrast, noble and virtuous people dread even the arrogant delusion ('cerukku') that makes one think they can commit an evil deed and escape its effects. The poet uses 'cerukku' to highlight that committing evil stems from a false sense of pride and mental blindness, which the wise carefully avoid.
